newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil static, seeks direction from crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil static, seeks direction from crude.

text.p: Activity and prices stagnated for high and low sulphur cracked fuel in NWE on Friday as the market digested the latest dip in crude prices.
Barge business was restricted by a lack of physical bunker demand. No more than 10,000 tonnes was seen, the bulk of which was represented by two large enquiries.
"It's been very quiet, with uncertain direction," said a trader. Deals were seen between $113-115 fob ARA a tonne.
High sulphur cracked cargoes held steady around $108 fob NWE although prices were expected to improve marginally next week on the back of thinner Russian straight-run material.

But any Russian tariffs levied on exports would have to be high enough to persuade Russian material to stay at home rather than seek external buyers. End-users continue to feel the prices are too high and appear relaxed enough to back this up by not buying.

Low sulphur fuel drifted sideways after the recent bounce up, but sellers with material continue to hold out for prices close to $128-130 cif NWE. Although material was likely to become harder to find with cold weather in the U.S. expected to draw in material, product was still heard on offer below the published quotes late on Friday. -- London +44 171 542 8980
